text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Public servants and local authorities are to receive a pay increase backdated to January 1 and retired people and war veterans will also get an increase in their pensions. The minimum monthly salary for a civil servant will rise to 144,000 ($12.87) from ($10.72). The decision includes a 20-percent hike in the monthly pension for those who qualify for state social insurance.
-- Consumer prices rose 0.8 percent in January.
-- The government has delared a moratorium on licenses for beer and soft drink joint ventures.
-- The Ministry of Education and Training believes that its budget will be roughly $910 million short of needs by 2000.
-- Vietnam Social Insurance organisation has reported that violations within the system have brought losses of up to $90.9 million every year for the State.
-- The Communist Party's Politburo issued a directive to reinforce the country's offensive against corruption. - - - -
-- The Ministry of Transport has been granted a license for a $71.4 million project to upgrade waterways linking Ho Chi Minh City with Ca Mau and Kien Luong in the south Mekong Delta.
-- The United Nations Development Programme's new country representative, Edouard Wattez, began his assignment in Vietnam on Monday.
